newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila gets $2.9 bln in pledges from donors.
newsitem.headline: Manila gets $2.9 bln in pledges from donors.

text.p: The Philippines won aid pledges worth $2.9 billion at an annual meeting of donor nations on Wednesday, the World Bank said.
Japan was the country's biggest supporter, pledging $1.4 billion, the World Bank's Manila representative office said in a statement on the donor's meeting held in Tokyo on Wednesday.
Donors, however, warned the Philippines against complacency and urged it to address its current account deficit, improve tax collection and increase domestic savings.

"The donors called on the Philippines to strengthen the economy's resilience to external shocks, particularly in view of the rising trade and current account deficits, and the increased reliance on potentially volatile capital inflows," the World Bank said.

The World Bank chaired the sixth annual consultative meeting of the Philippine Assistance Programme (PAP), launched in 1989 to help restructure the Philippine economy. Before the meeting, the Philippine government had said it expected $2.55 billion in new aid pledges.

The World Bank said donor nations praised the Philippine government on its strong economic management, which resulted in a gross national product growth accelerating to an annual 7.1 percent in the first three quarters of this year from 0.5 percent in 1991.
